## Summary

Exit zero from tmux proves bytes moved, not that the agent accepted them — pij had to add composer polling for exactly this. GATED ON oq-0004: whether the standing never-capture-pane constraint binds product code or only agents and tests. Built last so that answer can arrive late.

INHERITED FROM PHASE 2, do not rediscover: (1) Any new websocket control frame MUST be added to CONTROL_TYPES in hooks/use-terminal-socket.ts — a frame missing from that Set is not rejected, it is written into xterm as terminal data and prints raw JSON into the user's terminal. (2) The send-keys branch sits inside the JSON.parse try in terminal-ws.ts; an escaping throw falls through to pty.write(data), so assert nothing reaches the pty even when the runner throws. | tk-0202 | At-most-once re-press, and the negative half of honest UI state | 064-terminal | ph-0003 | [x] checked | — | — | [x] 3/3 [tk-0202](#tk-0202) | Enter is re-pressed at most 3 times at 250ms while a payload is still pending, the payload is NEVER retyped, and no success is ever signalled from an exit code alone. | BUILDABLE NOW — independent of oq-0004. Two halves, and only the negative one is in scope until the pane read is ruled. (1) AT-MOST-ONCE: re-press Enter up to 3 times at 250ms, NEVER retype the payload after the first Enter — retyping is how a prompt gets double-submitted, and at-most-once beats speculative replay (workshop 001 section 2). Without the pane read there is no pending signal to drive the retry, so build the mechanism and its policy with the signal injected, so tk-0201 can supply it later without reshaping this. (2) THE NEGATIVE HALF OF HONEST UI: assert that nothing claims success from a zero exit code. Phase 2 deliberately ships no success signal — terminal-inner toasts on failure only — and this task must keep it that way rather than adding one. Exit 0 proves bytes moved, not that the agent accepted them (workshop 001 section 5). INHERITED FROM PHASE 2: any new websocket control frame MUST be added to CONTROL_TYPES in hooks/use-terminal-socket.ts or it is written into xterm as terminal data and prints raw JSON into the user terminal; and the send-keys branch sits inside the JSON.parse try in terminal-ws.ts, so an escaping throw falls through to pty.write. | [ac-0014](../../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) |
